exposure: Rate of ventricular progression (≥3 mm/week vs. <3 mm/week)
cohort: Fetuses with isolated severe fetal ventriculomegaly (ISVM)
finding: Fetuses with ISVM and ventricular growth of ≥3 mm/week (accelerators) were more likely to require postnatal VP shunting, were delivered at earlier gestational ages, and were more likely to be born by planned cesarean section compared to fetuses with ventricular growth <3 mm/week (plateaus).
mod_finding: Plateaus were significantly more likely to undergo a trial of labor while accelerators were more likely to have planned cesareans.
gest_age: Varied, based on time of delivery
